# The RNApipe map {#sec-pipeline-map}

Before going through the steps one at a time, here is the whole of bagPipes'
`RNApipe` at once. It is really **two workflows** run one after the other by
`RNApipe.sh`:

1. **`RNApipeCore`** (`workflows/RNApipeCore.snakefile`) processes every
   sample on its own.
2. **`mergeSignal`** (`workflows/mergeSignal.snakefile`) pools replicates
   into merged BAMs and tracks.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  R["Raw FASTQ<br/>R1 + R2 per sample"] --> FQ["fastqc<br/>(FastQC)"]
  R --> TR["trim<br/>(Trim Galore)"]
  TR --> QU["quant<br/>(Salmon)"]
  TR --> AL["align<br/>(HISAT2 + samtools)"]
  AL --> SI["signal<br/>(bamCoverage, unstranded)"]
  AL --> SS["strandedSignal<br/>(bamCoverage fwd / rev)"]
  QU --> TX["tximport<br/>(R)"]
  FQ & TR & QU & AL & SI & SS --> MQ["multiqc"]
  AL -.-> MA["mergeAlign<br/>(samtools merge)"]
  MA -.-> MS["mergeSignal /<br/>mergeStrandedSignal"]

  classDef core fill:#e8f1fa,stroke:#2c7bb6;
  classDef merge fill:#fdf3e7,stroke:#d98b2b,stroke-dasharray: 4 3;
  class FQ,TR,QU,AL,SI,SS,TX,MQ core;
  class MA,MS merge;
```

Blue boxes are `RNApipeCore`; dashed orange boxes are `mergeSignal`.

The two branches after trimming answer **different questions**:

| Branch | Question | Final product | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Salmon → tximport** | *How much* of each gene is there? | Gene-level count matrix (`_tximport.rds`) | Differential expression (DESeq2) |
| **HISAT2 → bamCoverage** | *Where* in the genome do the reads fall? | BAMs and bigWig tracks | Looking at data in IGV, figures, QC |

## Every rule in one table

| Rule | Tool (version) | Input | Output | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fastqc` | FastQC 0.12.1 | raw FASTQ | `QC/{sample}_R1/R2_fastqc.{html,zip}` | [FastQC](fastqc.qmd) |
| `trim` | Trim Galore 0.6.10 | raw FASTQ | `trim/{sample}_R1/R2_trimmed.fastq.gz` + reports | [Trimming](trimming.qmd) |
| `quant` | Salmon 1.10.3 | trimmed FASTQ | `quant/{sample}/quant.sf` | [Salmon](salmon.qmd) |
| `align` | HISAT2 2.2.1, samtools 1.22 | trimmed FASTQ | `align/{sample}_sorted.bam`, `.bai`, `_stats.txt` | [Alignment](alignment.qmd) |
| `signal` | deepTools 3.5.4 | BAM | `signal/unstranded/{sample}.bw` | [Signal tracks](signal-tracks.qmd) |
| `strandedSignal` | deepTools 3.5.4 | BAM | `signal/stranded/{sample}_fwd.bw`, `_rev.bw` | [Signal tracks](signal-tracks.qmd) |
| `multiqc` | MultiQC 1.28 | everything above | `QC/{runName}_multiqc_report.html` | [MultiQC](multiqc.qmd) |
| `tximport` | R 4.4.0 | all `quant.sf` + GTF | `quant/{runName}_tximport.rds` | [tximport](tximport.qmd) |
| `mergeAlign` | samtools | replicate BAMs | `mergeAlign/{mergeName}_sorted.bam` | [Merging](merging.qmd) |
| `mergeSignal`, `mergeStrandedSignal` | deepTools | merged BAM | `mergeSignal/...bw` | [Merging](merging.qmd) |

Versions are from `config/RNAconfig.yaml`.

## The output folder

```
output/
├── {runName}_RNApipeSamplesheet.txt   # your samplesheet + the sample names used
├── QC/                                # MultiQC report and its data folder
├── trim/                              # (emptied at the end, see below)
├── quant/{sample}/quant.sf            # Salmon, one folder per sample
├── quant/{runName}_tximport.rds       # the gene-level object for R
├── align/                             # sorted BAMs, indexes, flagstat
├── signal/unstranded/  signal/stranded/
├── mergeAlign/  mergeSignal/          # only if merging is on
├── logs/                              # each tool's own messages
├── logs_slurm/                        # SLURM's record of each job
└── benchmarks/                        # time and memory used by each step
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Where did my FastQC reports and trimmed FASTQs go?

In `RNApipeCore.snakefile` the FastQC files, trimming reports and trimmed
FASTQs are marked `temp()`. Snakemake **deletes them** once every rule that
needs them has finished (the last one is `multiqc`). Their numbers are
kept in `QC/{runName}_multiqc_data/` and in the MultiQC report. This saves a lot
of disk space. If you want to keep them, remove the `temp( )` wrapper around
those outputs.
:::
